records.label: Metric definition
records.description: Records what a measure includes and the question it answers.

chapters.label: Review and release an agreed change

fields.name: Measure
fields.description: The business quantity being defined.
fields.value: Percentage of deliveries due that arrived on time

fields.name: Counts as on time
fields.description: The comparison that qualifies a delivery.
fields.value: Delivered at or before the promised time

fields.name: Denominator
fields.description: The full population included in the calculation.
fields.value: All deliveries due by noon, including those not yet delivered

fields.name: Measured at
fields.description: The agreed reporting cutoff.

fields.name: Responsible team
fields.description: The team accountable for this definition.

fields.name: Source
fields.description: The table containing the delivery records.

records.interpretation: This is Delivery Operations’ all-due rule: two on time out of four due gives 50.0%. The incident’s Service Analytics report uses a different, completed-delivery definition.
records.limit: An agreed definition does not prove that a saved query or published output implements it.

records.label: Responsible team
records.description: Names who can explain and approve the meaning of a measure.

chapters.label: Review and release an agreed change

fields.name: Team
fields.description: The team responsible for the all-due meaning.

fields.name: Definition responsibility
fields.description: The specific agreement this team maintains.
fields.value: Confirm the denominator and original-promise rule

fields.name: Measure
fields.description: The measure whose meaning this team owns.
fields.value: Percentage of deliveries due that arrived on time

records.interpretation: Delivery Operations confirms which deliveries belong in the measure. Chapter 8 separately assigns Service Analytics the completed-delivery definition and the reporting engineer collection maintenance.
records.limit: A collected team name alone does not establish that the team accepted responsibility.

records.label: Dataset
records.description: Identifies a table and the kind of rows it contains.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The SQLite table name.

fields.name: type
fields.description: The object kind recorded by SQLite.

fields.name: Row represents
fields.description: The unit described by each source row.

fields.name: Columns
fields.description: The fields declared by the source SQL.

records.interpretation: The schema describes the source table used by the saved view and the incident’s retained inputs. The book also describes a different dataset, prod/parcels/delivery_summary, which receives published summaries.
records.limit: The current table does not establish which rows a historical run read.

records.label: Column
records.description: Describes one field’s declared type and constraints.

chapters.label: Debug a successful but incorrect calculation

fields.name: name
fields.description: The declared column name.

fields.name: type
fields.description: The type declared in SQLite.

fields.name: notnull
fields.description: Whether SQLite requires a value: 0 permits NULL.

fields.name: pk
fields.description: Position in the primary key: 0 means not a key column.

fields.name: Table
fields.description: The table containing this column.

records.interpretation: The database allows delivered_at to be NULL. In this complete teaching example, that marks a parcel that has not yet arrived; the declaration alone does not supply that meaning.
records.limit: A column name and type cannot establish whether a timestamp records depot arrival or customer delivery.

records.label: Saved query
records.description: Retains the SQL definition of a named calculation.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The saved view’s name.

fields.name: type
fields.description: The object kind recorded by SQLite.

fields.name: Source
fields.description: The table read by this SQL.

fields.name: Filter
fields.description: The condition that removes unfinished parcels.

fields.name: Denominator
fields.description: The count after applying the filter.

records.interpretation: The view counts completed deliveries. With the four 13:00 teaching rows it returns 66.7%, whereas Delivery Operations’ all-due rule requires 50.0%.
records.limit: Reading a saved query explains its calculation but does not establish the business rule the reader needs.
records.code:
CREATE VIEW on_time_completed AS
SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS completed,
    SUM(CASE WHEN delivered_at <= promised_at THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS on_time,
    ROUND(
        100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN delivered_at <= promised_at THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
        / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0),
        1
    ) AS percentage
FROM deliveries
WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL;

records.label: Job
records.description: Describes a repeatable process that calculates and saves a result.

fields.name: job_name
fields.description: The process name used by the simulation’s run records.

fields.name: Input
fields.description: The source records captured before each run.

fields.name: Purpose
fields.description: What this scheduled process produces.
fields.value: Save the completed-delivery percentage for Delivery performance

records.interpretation: The same job has several executions with different inputs and outcomes. Its R1205 execution succeeded; the later R1230 execution failed before publication.
records.limit: A job-level dependency identifies a route but cannot identify which execution supplied a displayed number.

records.label: Run
records.description: Records one execution, its outcome, and the input and code it used.

chapters.label: Debug a successful but incorrect calculation

fields.name: run_id
fields.description: The identifier of this execution.

fields.name: job_name
fields.description: The job that was executed.

fields.name: status
fields.description: The recorded execution outcome.

fields.name: input_snapshot_id
fields.description: The retained input this execution read.

fields.name: code_version
fields.description: The retained SQL this execution ran.

fields.name: finished_at
fields.description: The completion timestamp in UTC.

records.interpretation: R1205 used S1205 and completed-v1 to publish the 100.0% output. This reference chain explains the calculation that supplied the 13:00 refresh.
records.limit: A successful run alone does not prove that a later report refresh read its output.

records.label: Input snapshot
records.description: Identifies a retained copy of the source rows read by a run.

fields.name: snapshot_id
fields.description: The identifier of the retained input copy.

fields.name: captured_at
fields.description: When the input was copied, in UTC.

fields.name: row_count
fields.description: The number of rows originally captured.

records.interpretation: S1205 contains four parcels, with only D101 and D103 completed. Its retained rows are input data; the capture time, identifier and run reference are metadata about that input.
records.limit: A snapshot identifier without the retained rows cannot reproduce the historical calculation.

records.label: Code version
records.description: Retains the exact calculation associated with a historical execution.

chapters.label: Debug a successful but incorrect calculation

fields.name: code_version
fields.description: The version identifier stored by the simulation.

fields.name: Calculation
fields.description: Plain-language summary of the retained SQL shown below.
fields.value: Completed deliveries only; on-time count divided by completed count

fields.name: Filter
fields.description: The retained condition that excludes unfinished parcels.

records.interpretation: Executing this retained SQL against S1205 yields two completed deliveries, both on time: 100.0%. It implements Service Analytics’ completed-delivery rule.
records.limit: A version label without its retained code cannot establish which calculation ran.
records.code:
SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS completed,
    SUM(CASE WHEN delivered_at <= promised_at THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS on_time,
    ROUND(
        100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN delivered_at <= promised_at THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
        / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0),
        1
    ) AS percentage
FROM deliveries
WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL;

records.label: Published output
records.description: Records a saved result and the execution that produced it.

chapters.label: Distinguish an output version from a dataset

fields.name: output_version
fields.description: The identifier of this saved output.

fields.name: run_id
fields.description: The execution that produced this result.

fields.name: completed
fields.description: The completed deliveries included in the calculation.

fields.name: on_time
fields.description: The included deliveries at or before their promise.

fields.name: percentage
fields.description: The calculated percentage.

fields.name: published_at
fields.description: When this output was published, in UTC.

records.interpretation: This result was produced at 12:05 and read by F1300 at 13:00. The later R1230 failure left this earlier output available to the report.
records.limit: A published percentage does not establish that its definition fits the meeting’s question.

records.label: Report refresh
records.description: Records which saved output a report read at a particular time.

chapters.label: Check which version reached the report

fields.name: refresh_id
fields.description: The identifier of this report refresh.

fields.name: report_name
fields.description: The report that refreshed.

fields.name: refreshed_at
fields.description: When the report read its saved result, in UTC.

fields.name: output_version
fields.description: The exact output read by this refresh.

records.interpretation: The 13:00 refresh read the output published at 12:05, so it displayed 100.0%. Refreshing the report did not rerun the calculation.
records.limit: A recent refresh timestamp does not establish that its input was recently produced.

records.label: Data contract
records.description: Records the versioned agreement between a data producer and its consumers: what will be supplied, when, and how changes are handled.

chapters.label: Review and release an agreed change

fields.name: Contract
fields.description: The identifier of this contract version.

fields.name: Dataset
fields.description: The table whose snapshots the agreement covers.

fields.name: Producer
fields.description: The role responsible for supplying the snapshots and investigating failed checks.

fields.name: Consumers
fields.description: The teams that agree to the supplied data and review changes.

fields.name: Structure
fields.description: The declared fields and agreed timestamp representation.
fields.value: delivery_id TEXT; promised_at TEXT; delivered_at TEXT. Timestamps: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM in UTC.

fields.name: Meaning
fields.description: The meaning consumers rely on, beyond names and types.
fields.value: One row per delivery. promised_at is the original customer promise; an unfinished delivery has no completion time.

fields.name: Identifier rule
fields.description: The versioned uniqueness rule included in this contract.

fields.name: Required values
fields.description: Additional completeness requirements; delivered_at may be missing for an unfinished delivery.
fields.value: Identifiers and promised times must be present.

fields.name: Delivery commitment
fields.description: The cutoff and deadline; a check timestamp alone cannot prove delivery by this deadline.
fields.value: A daily snapshot of records known at 13:00 UTC, available by 13:05 UTC.

fields.name: Changes
fields.description: The review required before consumers receive a changed interface.
fields.value: Agree changes to structure or meaning with both consuming teams before publishing a new contract version.

records.interpretation: Both teams can use the same original-promise field while choosing different denominators. The agreement makes a switch to revised promises a change requiring consumer review.
records.limit: This is an invented agreement, not a guarantee implemented by the simulation. Check results and delivery evidence are needed to establish whether its commitments were met.

records.label: Quality rule
records.description: States a versioned expectation to check against data, such as the absence of duplicate identifiers.

chapters.label: Distinguish a rule from a result

fields.name: Rule
fields.description: The identifier of the rule version used in the review.

fields.name: Dataset
fields.description: The dataset to which this rule applies.

fields.name: Contract
fields.description: The agreement that includes this rule.

fields.name: Dimension
fields.description: The aspect of data quality this rule addresses.

fields.name: Scope
fields.description: The records within which uniqueness must hold; identifiers may recur across snapshots.

fields.name: Expectation
fields.description: The criterion used to judge the identifier check.
fields.value: No delivery_id appears in more than one row; expected duplicate count: zero.

records.interpretation: The same rule can be checked on many snapshots, producing a separate result each time. Recording its version makes past results interpretable if the rule later changes.
records.limit: The rule is an expectation, not evidence of a pass. Required values, accurate timestamps, freshness and suitability for a particular metric need their own evidence.

records.label: Quality check result
records.description: Records what checks found on a named input, when they ran, and which rule version the identifier check used.

fields.name: Source
fields.description: The table and teaching input actually reviewed.

fields.name: Scope
fields.description: The population included in this review.
fields.value: All four parcels due by noon

fields.name: Checked at
fields.description: The review time in UTC.

fields.name: Identifier rule
fields.description: The rule version evaluated by the identifier check; the time checks address separate requirements.

fields.name: Identifier check
fields.description: The result of checking uniqueness.
fields.value: Four rows, four distinct delivery identifiers

fields.name: Time checks
fields.description: The result of the recorded timestamp checks.
fields.value: Four promised times present; one delivery time empty, allowed for an unfinished parcel

records.interpretation: The review found four rows and four distinct delivery identifiers, meeting delivery-ids-unique-v1 for decision-input-1300. It also found all promised times present. This is the four-parcel 13:00 teaching input, separate from retained snapshot S1205.
records.limit: These checks establish neither timestamp accuracy, delivery by the contract deadline, the correct denominator, nor which input reached a report.

records.label: Source observation
records.description: Preserves a source’s claim and when a collector observed it.

fields.name: Dataset identifier
fields.description: The production summary dataset described by this observation.

fields.name: Source
fields.description: The system supplying the structural claim.

fields.name: Claim
fields.description: What the collector actually observed.

fields.name: Observed at
fields.description: When the source was checked, in UTC.

fields.name: Collected at
fields.description: When the catalogue received the observation, in UTC.

records.interpretation: The scan supports a structural claim about delivery_summary on 20 October. It is separate from the 19 October incident and does not identify the run that produced the table’s values.
records.limit: This observation describes delivery_summary, whereas the Dataset card’s example is deliveries; its observation time is not a creation time.

records.label: Collection run
records.description: Records the scope and timing of a collector’s work.

fields.name: Collector
fields.description: The collector whose work is being described.

fields.name: Scope
fields.description: The dataset explicitly described by the chapter’s observation.

fields.name: Observed at
fields.description: When the collector checked the database, in UTC.

fields.name: Collected at
fields.description: When its observation reached the catalogue, in UTC.

fields.name: Collected claim
fields.description: The structural observation supplied by this scan.

records.interpretation: This card models the scan described in Chapter 5; it is not an additional SQLite simulation table. A collection process preserves observations while its scope and outcome determine how omissions can be interpreted.
records.limit: One observed column does not prove a complete scan, and missing from a scan does not by itself mean deleted.

records.label: Decision
records.description: Records a chosen rule, the remaining evidence gap and who acts next.

chapters.label: Review and release an agreed change

fields.name: Decision
fields.description: The rule selected for the operations meeting.
fields.value: Use the all-due rule; expected four-parcel result: 50.0%

fields.name: Current gap
fields.description: The evidence still missing before the measure can be used.
fields.value: No verified all-due publication is attached

fields.name: Next action and owner
fields.description: The person and work needed to close that gap.
fields.value: Reporting engineer verifies the calculation and attaches the published output identifier and report refresh evidence before the next meeting

fields.name: Definition owner
fields.description: The team confirming the agreed meaning.
fields.value: Delivery Operations confirms the denominator and original-promise rule

records.interpretation: The decision selects the all-due definition and makes the publication gap explicit. Chapter 8 records a separate decision about how to maintain the evidence.
records.limit: This meeting decision remains pending until the calculation and publication are verified; the incident’s completed-delivery output does not close the gap.

records.label: Access decision
records.description: Records an approved purpose, scope and the controls that must implement it.
records.evidence: Illustrative policy decision; enforcement not tested

fields.name: Dataset
fields.description: Dataset whose access is being decided.

fields.name: Classification
fields.description: Handling category; a label does not enforce permissions.

fields.name: Permitted purpose
fields.description: Approved use, separate from technical read permission.

fields.name: Readers
fields.description: Identities eligible for scoped access.

fields.name: Approval
fields.description: Decision maker for purpose and scope; separate from the metric definition owner role.

fields.name: Controls
fields.description: Controls that operators must apply and verify.
fields.value: Identity group, scoped database reads, catalogue visibility and managed exports

fields.name: Review trigger
fields.description: When the decision needs reassessment.
fields.value: Purpose change, role change or approval expiry

records.interpretation: The decision connects an allowed use to responsible people and required controls. Effective grants and access tests are still needed to show enforcement.

records.label: Reuse description
records.description: Describes a dataset version so another reader can find, cite and assess its reuse conditions.

chapters.label: Read the planned FAIR publication record

fields.name: Dataset version
fields.description: A separate synthetic research dataset, not the operational deliveries table.

fields.name: Identifier status
fields.description: A repository would assign a persistent identifier; no deposit has occurred.

fields.name: Citation
fields.description: Planned citation; persistent identifier remains pending.
fields.value: Example Research Team (2026). Synthetic delivery measures, version 1.0. Example Repository.

fields.name: License and access
fields.description: Proposed reuse terms, subject to release approval.
fields.value: Proposed CC BY 4.0; planned public HTTPS download

fields.name: Provenance
fields.description: Origin and method claimed by this teaching example.
fields.value: Invented parcels; generator version 1.0; no customer records

fields.name: Meaning
fields.description: Population, time convention and missing-value meaning.
fields.value: All deliveries due by noon against original promises; UTC; missing completion means unfinished

fields.name: Machine-readable description
fields.description: A plan, not evidence of a schema-valid repository deposit.
fields.value: Planned DataCite properties and versioned field dictionary

records.interpretation: This separate synthetic example describes the information needed for discovery and reuse. FAIR principles do not by themselves establish quality, publication approval or legal compliance.
